sections.title: Fixed
items: **Undo could undo the wrong operation.** A message with Undo stays on screen while the pointer is on it, so after two changes in a row two of them could be stacked, and Undo on the older one put back the files of an operation that was no longer the last. Now only the last operation has Undo, and only until you move on: a click anywhere else in the page, or the next change, takes the message with Undo away. The button names what it undoes (**Undo: GitHub settings of Work**), and if something else was done in the meantime, in another tab or by cc-profiles itself, it asks first, with the same warning as Backups → **Restore**.

sections.title: Added
items: Profiles → GitHub shows, under each profile's fields, who its commits go out as now, with a ✓ when the email is the account's address, and a warning with **Use <account>'s** when it is not: an identity changed by mistake shows up there instead of in the history of your projects.

sections.title: Fixed
items: `install.sh` stopped on a new Mac, with "pipx, uv or Homebrew is required". With none of them it now installs uv first, with uv's official installer, in `~/.local/bin` (no `sudo`), and installs cc-profiles with it, on uv's own Python: neither Python nor Apple's developer tools are needed.
`install.sh` with uv installs cc-profiles on uv's own Python, which Homebrew updates cannot remove (`UV_PYTHON` still chooses another).

`install.sh` said which version it installed or updated from by asking the first `cc-profiles` in the `PATH`, which could be another, older copy: it now asks the copy it installed, and warns when your terminal would run another one first.

sections.title: Changed
items: `install.sh` refuses to run with `sudo` (on macOS it would fill your home folder with files owned by root), runs nothing if its download was cut short, says how to open the Mac app, and, when Claude Code is not installed, how to install it.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Opened from the Mac app, cc-profiles said "Claude Code is installed, but your terminal cannot find it" although the terminal found it: apps opened from the Finder or the Dock get a minimal `PATH` from macOS, without the lines of `~/.zshrc`, and cc-profiles looked there. It now asks your login shell for the `PATH` a new terminal gets. The same went for the note that `~/.local/bin` is not in your `PATH` after creating or importing a profile.

sections.title: Added
items: **Browser for Claude**, in Skills and MCP servers: add a **local browser** (Playwright's MCP server, `npx @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated`) to a profile or to all of them, a Chrome that Claude Code starts on this computer with a clean profile, so nothing goes through the claude.ai account; and turn off **Claude in Chrome at start** (Enabled by default in `/chrome`) in a profile or in all. Claude in Chrome reaches Claude Code through the account, so people sharing one can drive each other's browser; the section explains it, and warns when Chrome connects at start in profiles of more than one account, since the extension serves one at a time.

sections.title: Changed
items: The plugin's `/cc-profiles:open` has Claude run `cc-profiles open` with its Bash tool, which asks for permission the first time, instead of running it by itself: the Claude plugin directory accepts commands that run by themselves only from Verified organizations. `/cc-profiles`, added by the app, still opens it at once.

sections.title: Added
items: A **Privacy** page in the documentation: what cc-profiles reads, what it keeps on your computer, and the services it talks to. The plugin links it (`privacyPolicyUrl`).

sections.title: Fixed
items: The README and the Health guide said cc-profiles reaches only PyPI and the Claude Code installer: they now also list Anthropic (the plan limits, with each profile's own sign-in) and GitHub's public API (commit identities).

sections.title: Changed
items: The plugin's listing shows its name as cc-profiles, in lowercase, with keywords to find it.

sections.title: Changed
items: The plugin's description says what cc-profiles does and that it needs the cc-profiles app, installed with pipx, uv or Homebrew: the plugin only opens it.

sections.title: Changed
items: `/cc-profiles` (and the plugin's `/cc-profiles:open`), when cc-profiles is not installed, suggests `pipx`, `uv` or Homebrew instead of a `curl … | sh` line. The plugin has an icon and a link to its repository, for the Claude plugin directory.

sections.title: Added
items: **Automatic export**, in the About panel: every profile exported every day or every week, conversations included and never the login, into `iCloud Drive/cc-profiles exports` (or `~/.cc-profiles/exports`), keeping the last 3 of each. Off until you turn it on; **Export now** runs it at once, and the panel shows the last and next export.
A profile whose folder is gone can be put back from its latest export: **Restore from export…** in the Profiles tab, with Undo. The Mac app sends a notification when a profile's folder disappears.

sections.title: Fixed
items: **Import profile…** takes archives up to 2 GB: an export of a profile with its conversations easily passes the old 500 MB limit, which refused it.

A GitHub account renamed after signing in: the GitHub CLI keeps the old name, which may now belong to someone else. cc-profiles asks `gh` whose account it really is, suggests the commit identity of that account (not of whoever has the old name now), and the GitHub table says **renamed** with the new name and **Sign in again…**.

A new profile made from a base commits as its own GitHub account: the commit identity copied from a base signed in to another account is replaced by the new account's, and the message says so. A profile without an identity gets its account's right away, instead of at the next start.

A profile whose folder was removed outside cc-profiles: the Profiles tab marks it **folder missing** and says to put the folder back or delete the profile, which still works. Every change that involves it is refused with that message, before anything is written: it no longer fails halfway with a `FileNotFoundError`, leaves an incomplete backup or creates loose folders where the profile was, and the checks at start no longer leave a failed backup each time.

sections.title: Changed
items: Messages in the bottom right corner close sooner: after 3.5 seconds, 7 with **Undo**, 6 for errors (they were 6, 12 and 9). They still stay while the pointer or the focus is on them.
